questions.q: A tailor folds a sheet of tracing cloth 0.25 mm thick in half, again and again, 7 times in all. Each fold doubles the thickness. How thick is the folded pile?
questions.a: 32 mm

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: 7^3 and 3^7 have the same value, because both are made from the numbers 7 and 3.
Statement 2: p × p × q × q × q is written as p^2 q^3 and read as 'p squared q cubed'.
Statement 3: 0^6 = 0, because six zeros multiplied together give 0.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only

questions.q: A seed company packs 5 sachets in a pouch, 5 pouches in a box, 5 boxes in a carton and 5 cartons in a crate. A shop in Nashik orders 5 crates. Which expression gives the number of sachets the shop receives?
When 7200 is written as a product of powers of primes in the form 2^a × 3^2 × 5^2, the exponent a = ___.
A class-test answer reads: 6 × 6 × 6 × 6 = 6^4 = 24. Which statement correctly describes the slip?
questions.a: It works out 6 × 4, not four 6s multiplied; 6^4 = 1296
o: It works out 6 × 4, not four 6s multiplied; 6^4 = 1296
The base and the exponent were swapped; the value is 4^6 = 4096
One 6 too few was written, so the value is really 6^3 = 216
Only the last step is wrong; the value is 6 × 6 × 4 = 144

questions.q:
Assertion (A): (-2)^5 × (-3)^3 is a negative number.
Reason (R): A product of non-zero numbers is negative exactly when it has an odd number of negative factors.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q: In a dictation round, the teacher reads out: 'seven raised to the power four, times two cubed'. Which expression should the students write, and what is its value?
Without multiplying out, decide which one of these products has a NEGATIVE value.

Match each situation in Column A with the expression in Column B that counts it.
Column A
1. Rupees in 10 bundles, each of 10 packets of 10 one-rupee coins
2. How many times bacteria multiply in 10 hours if they double every hour
3. Lotuses after 3 days if 1 lotus triples every day
4. Outfits from 3 shirts and 10 trousers
Column B
a. 3 × 10
b. 10^3
c. 3^3
d. 2^10
(a) Write 2592 as a product of powers of its prime factors. (b) Using your answer to (a), say whether 2592 can be written as 6^k for some counting number k. Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 2592 = 2^5 × 3^4. (b) No. 6^k = 2^k × 3^k needs the same exponent on 2 and on 3, but here the exponents are 5 and 4.
s: Part (b): No, because 6^k needs equal exponents on 2 and 3

questions.q: True or False: 'Since 2^5 = 32 is greater than 5^2 = 25, a^b is always greater than b^a when a is smaller than b.' Give a reason.
questions.a: False. A counter-example: 2^3 = 8 but 3^2 = 9, so here a^b is smaller than b^a even though 2 < 3.

questions.q: (a) Write 1296 as a product of powers of its prime factors. (b) Using your answer to (a), write 1296 as a power of 6 and also as a power of 36.
s: Part (b): 6^4 and 36^2, using the equal exponents

questions.q: (a) Find the values of 2^10 and 10^3, and say which is larger. (b) 2^20 is twenty 2s multiplied, that is (ten 2s) × (ten 2s). Without finding 2^20, use (a) to decide whether 2^20 is more or less than 10 lakh (10^6).
questions.a: (a) 2^10 = 1024 and 10^3 = 1000, so 2^10 is larger. (b) 2^20 = 1024 × 1024 and 10^6 = 1000 × 1000. Each factor 1024 is bigger than 1000, so 2^20 is more than 10 lakh. (Its value is 10,48,576.)
s: Part (b): 1024 × 1024 is more than 1000 × 1000, so 2^20 is more than 10^6

questions.q: Without multiplying out, find: (a) the sign of (-5)^7, with a reason; (b) the value of (-1)^99 + (-1)^100 + 0^5.
questions.a: (a) Negative: there are 7 factors of -5; pairs give positive products, and one -5 is left over. (b) (-1)^99 = -1, (-1)^100 = 1 and 0^5 = 0, so the sum is -1 + 1 + 0 = 0.
s: Part (a): negative, since an odd number of negative factors leaves one unpaired

questions.q:
A housing society in Pune has 1200 flats. Each flat needs 15 gate-pass codes a year, and no code may be used twice. The committee looks at three code plans (letters A to Z and digits 0 to 9 may repeat):
Plan X: 4 digits, for example 0739
Plan Y: 3 letters, for example KQB
Plan Z: 2 letters followed by 2 digits, for example MR42
(a) How many codes does Plan X give?
(b) How many codes does Plan Y give?
(c) How many codes does Plan Z give?
(d) How many codes are needed in a year, and which ONE plan should the committee choose? Justify.
s: Part (d): 18,000 needed; X and Y fall short, choose Z

questions.q: Estu's 5-slot safe has the digits 0 to 9 in each slot. He plans to buy a 6-slot lock that shows one of 20 symbols (the letters A to T) in each slot. His sister claims, 'The new lock has more than 500 times as many passwords as the old one.' Check the claim.
questions.a: The claim is right. Old lock: 10^5 = 1,00,000 passwords. New lock: 20^6 = 2^6 × 10^6 = 64 × 10,00,000 = 6,40,00,000 passwords. 6,40,00,000 ÷ 1,00,000 = 640, which is more than 500.
s: Divides to get 640 times and agrees with the claim

questions.q: Show that no power of 2 (2^1, 2^2, 2^3, ...) can ever end in the digit 0.
questions.a: A power of 2 is 2 × 2 × ... × 2, so its only prime factor is 2. A number ending in 0 is a multiple of 10 = 2 × 5, so it must have 5 as a prime factor. A power of 2 never has the factor 5, so it can never end in 0. (The units digits only cycle 2, 4, 8, 6.)
s: States that a power of 2 has only the prime factor 2
States that a number ending in 0 must have the factor 5 (10 = 2 × 5)
Concludes that no power of 2 ends in 0

questions.q: Write a real-life situation, with packing or sharing at several levels, whose answer is 4 × 3^5. Then find the answer and say what it counts.
questions.a: Example: 4 trucks each carry 3 containers, each container holds 3 crates, each crate 3 boxes, each box 3 packets and each packet 3 pens. Pens = 4 × 3^5 = 4 × 243 = 972. Any situation with a 4 and then five levels of 3 is acceptable.
s: A situation with one factor 4 and exactly five levels of 3
Says what the 972 counts in the situation

questions.q: In a school lab, Culture P starts with 3000 cells and gains 3000 cells every hour. Culture Q starts with 3 cells and doubles every hour. (a) Write an expression for the number of cells in each culture after h hours. (b) Find both counts after 10 hours. (c) After how many whole hours does Q first have more cells than P? (d) Compare the two after 20 hours: about how many times larger is the bigger culture? Explain which kind of growth wins in the long run.
questions.a: (a) P = 3000 + 3000h; Q = 3 × 2^h. (b) P = 33,000; Q = 3 × 1024 = 3072. (c) After 13 hours P = 42,000 and Q = 24,576; after 14 hours P = 45,000 and Q = 49,152, so after 14 hours. (d) P = 63,000 and Q = 3 × 2^20 = 31,45,728, about 50 times P. Multiplicative (exponential) growth overtakes additive (linear) growth however small it starts.
s: Part (d): 63,000 against 31,45,728, about 50 times, exponential wins

questions.q: Water hyacinth in a village pond doubles in area every day. It started as one plant on Day 0 and covered the whole pond on Day 24. (a) On which day was the pond half covered? (b) On which day was it one-quarter covered? (c) Write the number of plants on Day 24 as a power of 2 and find its value. (d) In a second pond, one plant on Day 0 triples every day. On which day does the second pond first have more plants than the first pond had on Day 24? Show your working.
questions.a: (a) Day 23, since the area doubles from half to full in one day. (b) Day 22. (c) 2^24 = 1,67,77,216. (d) 3^15 = 1,43,48,907 is less than 2^24 but 3^16 = 4,30,46,721 is more, so Day 16.
s: Part (a): Day 23 by working back one doubling
Part (d): compares 3^15 = 1,43,48,907 and 3^16 = 4,30,46,721 with 2^24 and answers Day 16

questions.q:
A false message about a school holiday spreads on phones in a town. One person sent it first, and every hour the number of people who have it triples. At 8 pm the school's IT team finds that 59,049 people have it. The local cyber cell says the message becomes very hard to stop once more than 1 crore people have it.
(a) Write 59,049 as a power of 3.
(b) At what time was the message first sent?
(c) What is the latest whole hour at which fewer than 1 crore people have the message? Give the counts that support your answer.
questions.a: (a) 59,049 = 3^10. (b) 10 hours before 8 pm, at 10 am. (c) At midnight (14 hours after 10 am) 3^14 = 47,82,969 people have it, under 1 crore; at 1 am 3^15 = 1,43,48,907, over 1 crore. So midnight is the latest hour.

questions.q: You are told that 2^6 = 64 and 2^5 = 32. (a) Find 2^11 using just one multiplication, and say which rule you used. (b) Write 2^11 as a product of two powers of 2 in a different way and check that it gives the same value.
questions.a: (a) 2^11 = 2^6 × 2^5 = 64 × 32 = 2048, using n^a × n^b = n^(a+b). (b) For example 2^8 × 2^3 = 256 × 8 = 2048 (any pair of exponents adding to 11).
s: Part (b): another pair with exponents adding to 11, checked to give 2048

questions.q:
Assertion (A): (5^3)^2 = 5^6.
Reason (R): (5^3)^2 means 5^3 × 5^3, and when powers of the same base are multiplied the exponents add: 3 + 3 = 6.
questions.a: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: In an inter-house maths quiz, one team writes 4^3 × 4^5 = 16^8 on its answer slate. The quizmaster asks the other teams for the correct answer. Which answer should he accept?

Damini puts 1 lotus in a pond where the number of lotuses doubles every day. After 5 days she moves all of them to a pond where the number triples every day, and leaves them there for 5 more days. Which expression gives the number of lotuses at the end?
Without multiplying out, the number 2^5 × 5^5 has ___ digits.

Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: (2^3)^4 and (2^4)^3 have the same value.
Statement 2: 3^2 × 3^5 = 9^7.
Statement 3: (-2)^3 × (-2)^2 = (-2)^5 = 32.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 only

questions.q:
A school is tiling its square foyer. Design 1: 16 panels by 16 panels, each panel a square of 16 tiles by 16 tiles. Design 2: 8 panels by 8 panels, each panel a square of 32 tiles by 32 tiles. Tiles come in packs of 2^8 tiles at Rs 450 a pack.
(a) Show that both designs use the same number of tiles, written as a power of 2.
(b) How many packs of tiles are needed, and what do they cost?
(c) Next year the school will tile a square hall whose side is 4 times the side of the foyer, using the same tiles. Write the number of tiles as a power of 2.
(d) The school has set aside Rs 4,60,800 for the hall's tiles, reasoning that 4 times the side needs only 4 times the foyer's cost. Is the budget enough? If not, by how much is it short?
questions.a: (a) Design 1: 16^2 × 16^2 = 16^4 = (2^4)^4 = 2^16. Design 2: 8^2 × 32^2 = (8 × 32)^2 = 256^2 = (2^8)^2 = 2^16. Both use 65,536 tiles. (b) 2^16 ÷ 2^8 = 2^8 = 256 packs; 256 × 450 = Rs 1,15,200. (c) 4 times the side gives 4 × 4 = 2^4 times the tiles: 2^16 × 2^4 = 2^20 tiles. (d) Packs = 2^20 ÷ 2^8 = 2^12 = 4096, costing 4096 × 450 = Rs 18,43,200. The budget is not enough: it is short by Rs 13,82,400 (4 times the side means 16 times the area, not 4 times).

questions.q: A teacher asks four students to write 2^12 as a power of a power. Which student's answer is NOT equal to 2^12?
A shopkeeper wants 36^3 ÷ 12^3 without a calculator. Using m^a ÷ n^a = (m ÷ n)^a, what value should he get?
True or False: '6^4 = 6^2 × 6^2 = 12^2.' Give a reason or the correct statement.
questions.a: False. 6^4 = 6^2 × 6^2 is right (2 + 2 = 4), but 6^2 × 6^2 = (6 × 6)^2 = 36^2, not 12^2: powers with the same exponent multiply their bases, they do not add them. 36^2 = 1296 = 6^4, while 12^2 = 144.

questions.q: (a) Write 12^5 ÷ 4^5 as a single power. (b) You are told 4^5 = 1024. Use your answer to (a) to find the value of 12^5.
(a) Write 8^5 × 2^3 as a single power of 2. (b) Hence find k if 8^5 × 2^3 = 4^k.
Simplify and write in exponential form: (a) p^4 × p^6 × p (b) (x^2 y^3)^4
s: Part (a): p^11, counting the lone p as p^1

questions.q: Decide whether each statement is Always true, Sometimes true or Never true, and justify. (a) The product of two fourth powers is a fourth power. (b) A sixth power is also a cube. (c) a^m × a^n = a^(m × n) for counting numbers m and n (take a = 2). (d) (a^m)^n = (a^n)^m.
questions.a: (a) Always: p^4 × q^4 = (pq)^4. (b) Always: a^6 = (a^2)^3. (c) Sometimes: the left side is 2^(m+n), so it holds only when m + n = m × n, for example m = n = 2 (2^2 × 2^2 = 16 = 2^4), but not m = 2, n = 3 (32 against 64). (d) Always: both equal a^(mn).
s: Part (c): Sometimes, with one case where it holds and one where it fails

questions.q: Kavya says: '3^2 × 3^3 = 3^5 = 243, and in the same way (3^2)^3 = 3^5 = 243.' Is she right? Check each part.
questions.a: She is partly right. 3^2 × 3^3 = 9 × 27 = 243 = 3^5 is correct. But (3^2)^3 = 3^2 × 3^2 × 3^2 = 3^6 = 729: for a power of a power the exponents multiply, not add.
s: Concludes she is partly right: exponents multiply for a power of a power

questions.q: Show that 2^7 cannot be written as (2^a)^b where a and b are both counting numbers greater than 1.
questions.a: (2^a)^b = 2^(a × b), so we would need a × b = 7. But 7 is prime: its only factor pairs are 1 × 7 and 7 × 1. So one of a, b must be 1, and it is impossible with both greater than 1.
s: Notes 7 is prime, factor pairs only 1 × 7
Concludes a or b must be 1

questions.q: You know 4^3 = 64 and 4^4 = 256. (a) Find 4^7 with a single multiplication. (b) Show that 2^14 = 4^7 using a power of a power. (c) Hence write down the value of 2^14 without any further multiplication.
Make up a real situation whose answer is (4^2)^3. Then show that the answer is also 4^6, and find its value.
questions.a: Example: a warehouse has 16 rooms, each room has 16 racks and each rack holds 16 boxes; boxes = 16 × 16 × 16 = (4^2)^3. Since (4^2)^3 = 4^2 × 4^2 × 4^2 = 4^(2+2+2) = 4^6 = 4096.
s: A situation with three levels of 16 (= 4^2)

questions.q: (a) Write 4^15 and 8^10 as powers of 2 and compare them. (b) Write 2^30 and 3^20 as powers with exponent 10, and decide which is greater. (c) A rule of thumb on a revision sheet says, 'The bigger exponent always gives the bigger number, so 2^30 is greater than 3^20.' Use (b) to judge this rule.
questions.a: (a) 4^15 = (2^2)^15 = 2^30 and 8^10 = (2^3)^10 = 2^30, so they are equal. (b) 2^30 = (2^3)^10 = 8^10 and 3^20 = (3^2)^10 = 9^10; since 9 > 8, 3^20 is greater. (c) The rule is wrong: the base matters too. 3^20 = 9^10 is greater than 2^30 = 8^10 even though 30 > 20.

questions.q:
A biology lab grows algae in two tanks. In Tank A the number of cells triples every day; in Tank B it doubles every day. Last term, a sample of 1 cell spent some days in Tank A and then the same number of days in Tank B, and ended with 46,656 cells.
(a) Write 46,656 as a power of 6.
(b) How many days did the sample spend in each tank? Explain using a rule of exponents.
(c) This term the lab has only 10 days in all and needs at least 20,000 cells. Tank A is costlier to run, so it wants the FEWEST days in Tank A. How many days should it use in each tank? Show the counts that decide it.
questions.a: (a) 46,656 = 6^6. (b) 3^k × 2^k = (3 × 2)^k = 6^k = 6^6, so 6 days in each tank. (c) With k days in A and 10 - k in B the count is 3^k × 2^(10-k): k = 7 gives 2187 × 8 = 17,496 (too few), k = 8 gives 6561 × 4 = 26,244. So 8 days in Tank A and 2 days in Tank B.
s: Part (c): 8 days in A and 2 in B, with 17,496 at 7 days and 26,244 at 8

questions.q: 64 is both a square (8^2) and a cube (4^3). Which of these numbers is also BOTH a square and a cube of a counting number?
A ribbon 2^9 cm long is cut in half and one half is kept. This is done 6 times in all. How long is the piece that is left?
questions.a: 8 cm

questions.q:
Assertion (A): 7^5 ÷ 7^5 = 1.
Reason (R): For n ≠ 0, n^a ÷ n^b = n^(a ÷ b).
questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: 2^100 ÷ 2^25 = 2^75.
Statement 2: (-3)^0 = -1, because the base is negative.
Statement 3: 10^6 ÷ 10^6 = 10^0 = 1.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q: Writing 4 as 2^2 first, the units digit of 2^150 ÷ 4^35 is ___.
A district library has 3^8 new books to share equally among 3^5 school libraries. How many books does each school library get?
A worked line in a notebook reads: 6^5 ÷ 6^2 = 1^3 = 1. What is the error, and what is the correct value?
questions.a: The base must stay 6, so the value is 6^3 = 216
o: The base must stay 6, so the value is 6^3 = 216
The exponents should be added, so the value is 6^7
The bases cancel, so the answer is the leftover exponent, 3

questions.q:
Match each expression in Column A with its value in Column B.
Column A
1. 6^8 ÷ 6^6
2. 9^0 × 4
3. 2^10 ÷ 2^4
4. 10^5 ÷ 10^5 + 10^0
Column B
a. 36
b. 4
c. 64
d. 2
On a power line for 3, Lata reads 3^9 = 19,683. Her friend asks, 'How many times larger is 3^9 than 9^2?' Using the rules of exponents, what should Lata answer?
A teacher writes (10^4 × 10^3) ÷ 10^7 on the board and four pupils give answers. Whose answer is correct?
questions.a: Anu: 1

questions.q: Sohan writes: '5^0 = 0, because no 5s are being multiplied. And by the same division rule, 0^4 ÷ 0^4 = 0^0 = 1.' Check both parts of what he writes.
questions.a: Both parts are wrong. 5^0 = 5^3 ÷ 5^3 = 125 ÷ 125 = 1, not 0. The division rule n^a ÷ n^b = n^(a-b) is stated only for n ≠ 0: 0^4 = 0, and dividing by 0 is not allowed, so the rule cannot be used on 0^4 ÷ 0^4 at all.
s: Explains that the rule needs n ≠ 0, since 0^4 = 0 and dividing by 0 is not allowed

questions.q: True or False: '(-8)^0 + 8^0 = 2.' Give a reason.
questions.a: True. Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 is 1, and -8 is non-zero, so (-8)^0 = 1 (not -1 or 0). Also 8^0 = 1, so the sum is 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.q: Find the missing exponent in each, showing the rule you use. (a) 5^k ÷ 5^3 = 625 (b) 2^10 ÷ 2^m = 1
Simplify, taking a and x as non-zero: (a) a^9 ÷ a^4 (b) (x^7 × x^3) ÷ x^10
(a) In the list 3^3 = 27, 3^2 = 9, 3^1 = 3, each value is the one before it divided by 3. Continue the list one more step to find 3^0. (b) Check your answer using the division rule on 3^5 ÷ 3^5.
(a) Write 25^4 as a power of 5. (b) Hence find the value of 25^4 ÷ 5^5.

A district inter-school cricket knockout starts with 128 = 2^7 teams. In every round the teams play in pairs and the losers leave, so the number of teams halves each round and a round has half as many matches as teams. Ground P can host 2^4 matches a day for Rs 30,000 a day; Ground Q can host 2^5 matches a day for Rs 50,000 a day. A new round always starts on a new day, and the tournament must finish within 10 days.
(a) How many teams are left after 3 rounds? Write it as a power of 2.
(b) How many rounds are needed to leave one champion? Use a power of 2 for the champion.
(c) How many matches are in Round 1, and how many days does Round 1 take on each ground?
(d) Which ground should the organisers book? Give the total days and cost for each ground.
questions.a: (a) 2^7 ÷ 2^3 = 2^4 = 16 teams. (b) One champion is 1 = 2^0 = 2^7 ÷ 2^7, so 7 rounds. (c) Round 1 has 2^7 ÷ 2 = 2^6 = 64 matches: Ground P needs 2^6 ÷ 2^4 = 2^2 = 4 days, Ground Q needs 2^6 ÷ 2^5 = 2 days. (d) The rounds have 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 matches. Ground P: 4 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11 days, Rs 3,30,000. Ground Q: 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8 days, Rs 4,00,000. P is cheaper but needs 11 days, more than the 10 allowed, so they should book Ground Q.
s: Part (c): 2^6 = 64 matches; 4 days on P, 2 days on Q
Part (d): P 11 days (Rs 3,30,000) breaks the 10-day limit; Q 8 days (Rs 4,00,000), book Q

questions.q: Show that 2^a ÷ 2^b, where a and b are counting numbers with a > b, can never equal 3.
questions.a: 2^a ÷ 2^b = 2^(a-b), and a - b is a counting number, so the result is one of 2, 4, 8, 16, ... Each of these is even (a product of 2s), while 3 is odd, and 3 is not a power of 2. So the quotient can never be 3.
s: Writes the quotient as 2^(a-b) with a - b a counting number
Notes every such power of 2 is even (2, 4, 8, ...)

questions.q: Without finding any large power, arrange P = 10^9 ÷ 10^6, Q = 2^25 ÷ 2^15 and R = 5^12 ÷ 25^4 in increasing order. Show each step.

(a) Simplify 7^12 ÷ 7^9 and find its value. (b) Simplify (5^3)^4 ÷ 5^10 and find its value. (c) Simplify (2^5 × 2^7) ÷ (2^4)^3. (d) A classmate writes the answer to (c) as 0, 'because the exponents cancel out'. Correct this. (e) Which of (a), (b), (c) has the largest value?

A school pen drive holds 2^34 bytes. One photo needs 2^21 bytes and one video needs 2^30 bytes. (a) How many photos alone would fill the drive? (b) How many videos alone would fill it? (c) If 2^3 videos are stored first, how many photos fit in the space that is left? (d) Mehul says, 'Deleting one video frees room for 9 photos, because 30 - 21 = 9.' Correct him.
questions.a: (a) 2^34 ÷ 2^21 = 2^13 = 8192 photos. (b) 2^34 ÷ 2^30 = 2^4 = 16 videos. (c) 2^3 videos use 2^3 × 2^30 = 2^33 bytes; 2^34 - 2^33 = 2^33 bytes are left, which hold 2^33 ÷ 2^21 = 2^12 = 4096 photos. (d) One video ÷ one photo = 2^30 ÷ 2^21 = 2^9 = 512, so it frees room for 512 photos; 9 is the exponent, not the number.

questions.q:
A state seed bank has 2^20 packets of millet seeds. It shares them equally among 2^5 districts. Each district shares its packets equally among 2^6 villages. In every village, each farmer needs 2^7 packets for one season.
(a) How many packets does each district get? Write it as a power of 2.
(b) How many packets does each village get?
(c) How many farmers in a village can get their full need?
(d) Kothur village has 6 farmers. Is its share enough? If not, how many more packets must it ask for?
questions.a: (a) 2^20 ÷ 2^5 = 2^15 = 32,768. (b) 2^15 ÷ 2^6 = 2^9 = 512. (c) 2^9 ÷ 2^7 = 2^2 = 4 farmers. (d) No: 6 × 128 = 768 packets are needed and the share is 512, so it must ask for 256 (= 2^8) more.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: 2^-3 = 1/8.
Statement 2: 5^-2 is greater than 5^-3.
Statement 3: 1/(10^-4) = 10^4.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1, 2 and 3

questions.q: A 10^2 kg sack of rice is split equally into 10 bags, each bag is split equally into 10 smaller bags, and this splitting into 10 is done 5 times in all. Using n^a ÷ n^b = n^(a-b), how heavy is one of the smallest bags? (1 kg = 1000 g)
questions.a: 1 g

questions.q:
A school science kit has a set of brass weights, one of each. Their labels are powers of 2 in grams:
2^3 g, 2^2 g, 2^1 g, 2^0 g, 2^-1 g, 2^-2 g, 2^-3 g.
Students use them on a beam balance, putting weights on one pan only.
(a) Write the mass of the 2^-2 g weight as a decimal.
(b) How many weights of 2^-3 g each would balance the 2^1 g weight?
(c) Which weights from the set together make exactly 5.375 g?
(d) A student wants to measure out exactly 0.6 g of salt using this set. Can the set do it? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 2^-2 = 1/4 = 0.25 g. (b) 2^1 ÷ 2^-3 = 2^4 = 16 weights. (c) 5.375 = 4 + 1 + 0.25 + 0.125 = 2^2 + 2^0 + 2^-2 + 2^-3. (d) No. Every combination is a whole number of eighths of a gram (the smallest weight is 2^-3 = 0.125 g), and 0.6 g is 4.8 eighths, not a whole number. The closest is 0.625 g = 2^-1 + 2^-3.
s: Part (d): No, since 0.6 g is not a whole number of eighths

questions.q:
Assertion (A): 10^-3 is a negative number.
Reason (R): 10^-3 = 1/10^3.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q: A class chart shows the power line for 7, with 7^2 = 49 and 7^-1 = 1/7. Ritu says 7^2 is 3 times 7^-1, 'because 2 - (-1) = 3'. Which is the correct comparison?
questions.a: 343 times as large
o: 3 times as large, as Ritu says

questions.q:
Match each expression in Column A with its value in Column B.
Column A
1. 2^-4 × 2^7
2. 3^2 × 3^-5 × 3^6
3. 10^-2 × 10^5
4. 5^-1 ÷ 5^-3
Column B
a. 8
b. 27
c. 1000
d. 25
Writing 25 as 5^2 first, the value of 5^-3 × 25^2 is ___.
On a worksheet, four expressions were meant to be copied as equal to 1/16, but one was copied wrongly. Which ONE is NOT equal to 1/16?
Neel says, 'The rule n^a × n^b = n^(a+b) still works with negative exponents. For example, 2^-2 × 2^5 = 2^3.' Check his example by writing 2^-2 as a fraction.
questions.a: Neel is right. 2^-2 = 1/4 and 2^5 = 32, so 2^-2 × 2^5 = 32/4 = 8 = 2^3, which is what the rule gives: -2 + 5 = 3.
s: Agrees with Neel: the rule gives -2 + 5 = 3

questions.q: True or False: 'Since 2^-1 = 1/2, any number with a negative exponent lies between 0 and 1.' Give a reason.
questions.a: False. A negative base can give a negative value: (-5)^-3 = 1/(-5)^3 = -1/125, which is less than 0. (Also (-2)^-1 = -1/2.)

questions.q: (a) Write 10^-5 as a fraction and as a decimal. (b) How many times smaller is 10^-5 than 10^-2?
Simplify and write in exponential form: (a) 10^-2 × 10^-5 (b) 6^-3 ÷ 6^-8
Kiran writes 1/(3^-4) = -81. (a) Find the correct value. (b) State the rule that Kiran missed.
questions.a: (a) 1/(3^-4) = 3^4 = 81. (b) n^a = 1/n^-a: a power with a negative exponent in the denominator moves to the numerator with a positive exponent. The minus sign is in the exponent, not in the value.
s: Part (b): states n^a = 1/n^-a (minus sign belongs to the exponent)

questions.q: Write 2^-6 as a product of two powers of 2 in each way: (a) one of the two factors is 2^4; (b) the two factors are equal.
(a) Find the value of each of 2^-3, 3^-2, 2^3 and 3^0. (b) Arrange them in increasing order.
Write a real situation whose answer is 2^-3 × 2^5. Then simplify it using a rule of exponents, find its value and say what it counts.
questions.a: Example: a sweet shop packs 2^5 = 32 boxes of laddoos, and each box weighs 2^-3 kg = 1/8 kg. Total mass = 2^-3 × 2^5 = 2^(-3+5) = 2^2 = 4 kg. Any situation with 2^5 equal items of size 2^-3 (or 2^5 parts each 1/8 of a unit) is acceptable.
s: A situation with 2^5 items each of size 2^-3 (1/8)
Says what the 4 measures (for example 4 kg in all)

questions.q: Simplify (2^-3)^2 × 4^4. Write each step as a power of 2, and say whether the answer is greater than or less than 1.
(a) Simplify p^4 q^10 ÷ (pq)^6 and write the answer using exponents (p, q ≠ 0). (b) Find its value when p = 2 and q = 3. (c) Show that your answer to (a) can also be written as (q^2 ÷ p)^2.
s: Part (a): expands (pq)^6 and gets p^-2 q^4

questions.q: A lab adds a tracer dye to a water sample; the amount of tracer halves every 6 hours. The first reading is 2^6 micrograms, and a reading is taken every 6 hours after that. (a) What is the amount after 12 hours? (b) Write the amount after 48 hours as a power of 2 and as a fraction. (c) The lab's meter can detect the tracer only while the amount is at least 2^-1 micrograms. At which reading time is it LAST detectable? (d) After how many hours will the reading be 2^-6 micrograms?
questions.a: (a) 2 halvings: 2^6 ÷ 2^2 = 2^4 = 16 micrograms. (b) 8 halvings: 2^6 ÷ 2^8 = 2^-2 = 1/4 microgram. (c) 2^6 ÷ 2^k ≥ 2^-1 needs 6 - k ≥ -1, so k ≤ 7: 7 halvings = 42 hours (2^-1 = 1/2 microgram); at 48 hours it is 1/4 microgram, too little. (d) 6 - k = -6 gives k = 12 halvings = 72 hours.
s: Part (c): 42 hours, with the 48-hour value below 2^-1

questions.q:
A school lab dilutes a coloured dye for a test. The starting dye has strength 1 unit. Each dilution mixes 1 part of the dye with 3 parts of water, so the strength becomes 1/4 of what it was. The test works only if the strength is less than 1/100 unit but more than 1/1000 unit.
(a) Write the strength after 2 dilutions as a power of 4 and as a fraction.
(b) An unlabelled tube has strength 1/1024 unit. How many dilutions has it had?
(c) How many dilutions should the lab make for the test? Show why one fewer and one more would not work.
questions.a: (a) 4^-2 = 1/16 unit. (b) 1024 = 4^5, so 1/1024 = 4^-5: 5 dilutions. (c) 4 dilutions: 4^-4 = 1/256, which lies between 1/1000 and 1/100. 3 dilutions give 1/64 (stronger than 1/100) and 5 give 1/1024 (weaker than 1/1000).

questions.q: A bank cashier must write the amount Rs 3,05,060 in expanded form using powers of 10 on a training sheet. Which form should she write?
True or False: 'In the expanded form of 50.05, the two 5s are worth 5 × 10^1 and 5 × 10^2.' Give a reason or the correct statement.
questions.a: False. The first 5 is 5 × 10^1, but the second 5 is two places after the decimal point, so it is 5 × 10^-2 (5 hundredths). 50.05 = 5 × 10^1 + 5 × 10^-2.

questions.q: In the number 7,08,213.46, the digit 8 is worth 8 × 10^m and the digit 4 is worth 4 × 10^n. Then m - n = ___.

Assertion (A): In 30.03, the left 3 is worth 1000 times the right 3.
Reason (R): Moving one place to the right divides a digit's value by 10, so the places 10^1 and 10^-2, which are three places apart, differ by a factor of 10^3.
questions.a: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: 5 × 10^2 + 3 × 10^0 = 530.
Statement 2: 0.07 = 7 × 10^-2.
Statement 3: One crore is 10^8.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 only

questions.q: A carpenter knows that 13^2 = 169. A square tile has a side of 0.13 m. What is its area?

While copying the number 6,072.5, a clerk shifts the digit 7 three places to the left. Correcting himself, he then shifts it five places to the right. Compared with its value in 6,072.5, the 7 is now worth its old value multiplied by
A lab notebook records a length in millimetres as 4 × 10^4 + 9 × 10^2 + 1 × 10^-1 + 5 × 10^-3. Which number is this?
In 4,40,404.04, the leftmost 4 is worth 4 × 10^5 and the rightmost 4 is worth 4 × 10^-2. The leftmost 4 is worth how many times the rightmost 4?
A news report says Company X earned Rs 2.5 billion last year and Company Y earned Rs 300 crore. A crore is 10^7 and a billion is 10^9. Which company earned more, and by how much?
questions.a: Company Y, by 50 crore

questions.q: (a) Write 2,04,300.06 in expanded form using powers of 10. (b) Which powers of 10 from 10^5 down to 10^-2 have the digit 0 as their coefficient?
15^2 = 225. (a) Write 0.15 as 15 × 10^k and use it to find (0.15)^2. (b) Find 1500^2 in the same way.

For a science-fair chart, Class 8 lists the lengths of four things in metres, written in expanded form:
Grain of rice: 6 × 10^-3
Pencil: 1 × 10^-1 + 8 × 10^-2
School bus: 1 × 10^1 + 2 × 10^0 + 5 × 10^-1
Cricket pitch: 2 × 10^1 + 1 × 10^-1 + 2 × 10^-2
(a) Without converting to decimals, which thing is the shortest and which is the longest? Give the reason from the powers of 10.
(b) How many rice grains placed end to end make one pencil length?
(c) For the chart, every length is multiplied by 10^-2. Write the chart lengths of the cricket pitch and the rice grain in metres.
(d) The chart is 1.5 m wide, and nothing shorter than 1 mm (10^-3 m) can be drawn. Is there any single factor 10^k that lets both the pitch and the rice grain be drawn on one chart? Justify.
questions.a: (a) The grain is shortest: its highest power is 10^-3, lower than everyone else's. The bus and the pitch both reach 10^1, and the pitch has 2 tens against the bus's 1, so the pitch is longest. (b) Pencil = 0.18 m, grain = 0.006 m: 0.18 ÷ 0.006 = 30 grains. (c) Pitch: 20.12 × 10^-2 = 0.2012 m; grain: 6 × 10^-3 × 10^-2 = 6 × 10^-5 m (0.06 mm). (d) No. The pitch fits only if 20.12 × 10^k ≤ 1.5, so k must be -2 or less (at 10^-1 it is 2.012 m). The grain can be drawn only if 6 × 10^-3 × 10^k ≥ 10^-3, so k must be 0 or more (at 10^-1 it is 0.6 mm). No k does both, so the class needs two charts or two scales.
s: Part (a): grain shortest (highest power 10^-3), pitch longest (2 × 10^1 against 1 × 10^1)
Part (d): No; pitch needs k ≤ -2, grain needs k ≥ 0

questions.q: The place values 1000, 100, 10 are 10^3, 10^2, 10^1. Moving one place right always divides by 10. Use this to explain (a) why the ones place is 10^0, and (b) why the tenths place is 10^-1.
(a) Write as a decimal number: (7 × 10^3) + (4 × 10^-1) + (9 × 10^-4). (b) How many digits does it have after the decimal point, and why?
questions.a: (a) 7000.4009. (b) Four, because the smallest power used is 10^-4, the fourth place after the point (the 2nd and 3rd places hold 0).

questions.q: Sana says: '0.3 × 10^2 + 0.3 × 10^-2 = 30.003. Also, 10^-2 means -100.' Check each part of what she says.

A worksheet answer gives 3 × 10^4 + 12 × 10^3 as the place-value expanded form of a number, the form in which each power of 10 is multiplied by a single digit from 0 to 9. Show that this cannot be the expanded form of any number, and write the correct expanded form of the number it adds up to.
questions.a: In an expanded form each power of 10 is multiplied by a single digit 0 to 9, because each place holds one digit; 12 is not a digit. The sum is 30,000 + 12,000 = 42,000, whose expanded form is 4 × 10^4 + 2 × 10^3.
s: States each coefficient must be one digit (0 to 9), so 12 × 10^3 is not allowed

questions.q: Make up a number whose expanded form uses exactly the powers 10^5, 10^2, 10^0 and 10^-2, each with a non-zero digit (and 0 in every other place), such that its digits add up to 20. Write the number and its expanded form.
questions.a: Example: 9,00,504.02 = 9 × 10^5 + 5 × 10^2 + 4 × 10^0 + 2 × 10^-2; digits 9 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 20. Any four non-zero digits adding to 20 in those places are acceptable.
s: Uses only the places 10^5, 10^2, 10^0, 10^-2 with zeros elsewhere

questions.q: Use: lakh = 10^5, crore = 10^7, kharab = 10^11, million = 10^6, billion = 10^9, trillion = 10^12. (a) How many lakhs make a billion? (b) How many millions make a crore? (c) The world has about 3 trillion trees. How many kharab is that? (d) A newspaper writes '20 lakh million'. Write it as a power of 10 multiplied by a single digit, and in crore.

A goldsmith weighs two chains: Chain P is 23.405 g and Chain Q is 23.45 g. (a) Write 23.405 in expanded form with powers of 10. (b) Write 23.45 in expanded form. (c) Compare the forms place by place: which chain is heavier, and by how much? Write the difference with powers of 10. (d) His helper says, 'They weigh the same, because both use the digits 2, 3, 4 and 5.' Judge this.
questions.a: (a) 2 × 10^1 + 3 × 10^0 + 4 × 10^-1 + 0 × 10^-2 + 5 × 10^-3. (b) 2 × 10^1 + 3 × 10^0 + 4 × 10^-1 + 5 × 10^-2. (c) They agree down to 10^-1; at 10^-2, Q has 5 and P has 0, so Q is heavier. Difference 23.45 - 23.405 = 0.045 g = 4 × 10^-2 + 5 × 10^-3. (d) Wrong: the value of a digit depends on its place (its power of 10), not just the digit; the 5 in Q is 5 × 10^-2 but in P it is 5 × 10^-3.
s: Part (d): rejects the claim, value depends on the power of 10

questions.q:
In a quiz, the clue card reads: 'My number is 5 × 10^3 + 0 × 10^2 + 7 × 10^1 + d × 10^0 + 3 × 10^-1, where d is a single digit. The sum of all my digits is 18. A second number, M, is 10^-2 times my number.' Two teams answer for M: Team A says 507.33 and Team B says 50,733.
(a) Find d.
(b) Write the number as a decimal.
(c) Find M, and decide which team (if either) is right, naming the slip each wrong team made.
questions.a: (a) 5 + 0 + 7 + d + 3 = 18, so d = 3. (b) 5073.3. (c) M = 5073.3 × 10^-2 = 5073.3 ÷ 100 = 50.733. Neither team is right: Team A divided by 10 only (moved each digit one place, as if 10^-1), and Team B multiplied by 10 instead of dividing (treated 10^-2 as if it were 10^1).
s: Part (c): M = 50.733, neither team right, slips named

questions.q: A district's population is printed as 4 × 10^6. In one copy, slip P changes the coefficient 4 to 5. In another copy, slip Q changes the exponent 6 to 7. Which statement is right?
questions.a: Q multiplies it by 10; P by only 1.25
o: Q multiplies it by 10; P by only 1.25
P multiplies it by 10; Q by only 1.25
Both slips add 1, so they change the number by the same amount
Q adds only 10 lakh people; P adds only 1 lakh people

questions.q: Written in scientific notation, (6 × 10^4) ÷ (8 × 10^-3) = 7.5 × 10^n, where n = ___.

Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: 0.00045 = 4.5 × 10^-4.
Statement 2: 36 × 10^5 is not in scientific notation.
Statement 3: 9.9 × 10^8 is greater than 1.1 × 10^9, because 9.9 is greater than 1.1.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): (2 × 10^3) × (3 × 10^4) = 6 × 10^7 is already in scientific notation.
Reason (R): When powers of 10 are multiplied, their exponents are added.
questions.a: A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
o: A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: There are about 5 × 10^14 Antarctic krill and about 8 × 10^9 people in the world. About how many krill are there for every person, in scientific notation?
Four reports write the number 30,80,00,000. Which report writes it correctly in scientific notation?

Match each number in Column A with its scientific notation in Column B.
Column A
1. 49,853
2. 24,30,000
3. 0.0243
4. 4,98,530
Column B
a. 2.43 × 10^6
b. 4.9853 × 10^4
c. 4.9853 × 10^5
d. 2.43 × 10^-2
Suppose 1.4 × 10^9 people each use about 8 × 10^1 litres of water for drinking and cooking in a month. What is the total in litres, written in scientific notation?

Four states report their rice output as: State P 0.5 × 10^8 kg, State Q 98 × 10^6 kg, State R 1.2 × 10^8 kg and State S 120 × 10^5 kg. After rewriting each in scientific notation, which amount is the SECOND-largest?
Under a school microscope a bacterium measures 0.000002 m long. About how many such bacteria, laid end to end, make 1 cm (10^-2 m)?
True or False: '9.9 × 10^4 is smaller than 1.01 × 10^5.' Give a reason.
questions.a: True. The exponent decides first: 9.9 × 10^4 = 99,000 while 1.01 × 10^5 = 1,01,000. Although 9.9 > 1.01, the second number has the larger exponent, so it is larger.

questions.q: (a) Write 7,20,000 and 0.0072 in scientific notation. (b) Using your answers, how many times larger is 7,20,000 than 0.0072?
questions.a: (a) 7.2 × 10^5 and 7.2 × 10^-3. (b) The coefficients are equal, so the ratio is 10^5 ÷ 10^-3 = 10^8 times.

questions.q: There are about 2 × 10^8 water buffaloes in the world. Suppose they all lived in herds of 500. (a) Write 500 in scientific notation. (b) Find the number of herds, in scientific notation.

Light travels about 3 × 10^8 m in one second. (a) How far does it travel in one minute? Write the answer in scientific notation. (b) The Sun is about 1.5 × 10^11 m from the Earth. About how many seconds does sunlight take to reach the Earth?
s: Part (a): 1.8 × 10^10 m, with the coefficient adjusted

questions.q: A tea-growing region has about 4 × 10^7 tea bushes, and each bush gives about 2.5 × 10^3 leaves in a season. (a) Multiply to find the total number of leaves. (b) Write your answer correctly in scientific notation, explaining any change you make.
s: Part (b): 1 × 10^11, since the coefficient must be below 10

questions.q: A newspaper adds two survey estimates, about 4.6 × 10^8 goats in one region and about 3.9 × 10^8 goats in another, and prints the total as 8.5 × 10^16. Check the printed total.
questions.a: The printed total is wrong. Both numbers have the same power 10^8, so their coefficients add: 4.6 × 10^8 + 3.9 × 10^8 = (4.6 + 3.9) × 10^8 = 8.5 × 10^8. The paper added the exponents (8 + 8 = 16), which is done only when multiplying powers.
s: Adds the coefficients with the same power: (4.6 + 3.9) × 10^8
Explains exponents add only when multiplying, so the claim is wrong

questions.q: A weather satellite's camera records without stopping for 5 × 10^5 seconds. Lalita says that this is less than 5 days. Check her claim (1 day = 86,400 seconds).
questions.a: Lalita is wrong. 5 × 10^5 ÷ 86,400 ≈ 5.8 days, which is more than 5 days. (Equivalently, 5 days = 5 × 86,400 = 4,32,000 s = 4.32 × 10^5 s, which is less than 5 × 10^5 s.)
s: Concludes the claim is wrong: it is more than 5 days

questions.q: Rekha multiplies 6 × 10^a by 7 × 10^b and writes the answer as 42 × 10^(a+b). Show that this cannot be the answer in scientific notation, whatever a and b are, and write the correct form.
questions.a: The product is 42 × 10^(a+b), but scientific notation needs a coefficient at least 1 and less than 10, and 42 is not less than 10 for any a and b. Since 42 = 4.2 × 10^1, the correct form is 4.2 × 10^(a+b+1).
s: States the coefficient must be at least 1 and below 10
Notes 42 breaks this whatever a and b are

questions.q: There are about 10^15 beetles in the world. Imagine counting them at 10 beetles every second, without stopping. Take 1 year ≈ 3.15 × 10^7 seconds. (a) How many seconds would the count take, in scientific notation? (b) About how many years is that? (c) The Himalayas are about 5.5 crore (5.5 × 10^7) years old. Is the counting time more or less than the age of the Himalayas, and about how many times?
questions.a: (a) 10^15 ÷ 10 = 10^14 seconds. (b) 10^14 ÷ (3.15 × 10^7) ≈ 3.17 × 10^6 years, about 32 lakh years. (c) Less: 5.5 × 10^7 ÷ 3.17 × 10^6 ≈ 17, so the Himalayas are about 17 times older than the counting time.

questions.q:
Class 8 is making a wall poster of the Sun and four planets. Their distances from the Sun are:
Mercury: 5.79 × 10^10 m
Venus: 1.082 × 10^11 m
Mars: 2.279 × 10^11 m
Jupiter: 7.785 × 10^11 m
The Sun is drawn at the left edge of a poster 60 cm wide. The class must choose one scale: 1 cm for every 10^10 m, 1 cm for every 2 × 10^10 m, or 1 cm for every 10^11 m.
(a) Write Mars's distance as an ordinary numeral with Indian commas.
(b) About how many times as far from the Sun as Mercury is Jupiter? Show the division with powers of 10.
(c) Using 1 cm for every 10^10 m, find the poster distances of Mars and Jupiter.
(d) The class wants all four planets on the poster, with Mercury at least 1 cm from the Sun. Which scale should it choose? Justify by checking all three.
questions.a: (a) 2,27,90,00,00,000 m. (b) 7.785 × 10^11 ÷ (5.79 × 10^10) = (7.785 ÷ 5.79) × 10^1 ≈ 1.34 × 10 ≈ 13 times. (c) Mars: 2.279 × 10^11 ÷ 10^10 = 22.79 cm; Jupiter: 7.785 × 10^11 ÷ 10^10 = 77.85 cm. (d) At 1 cm per 10^10 m Jupiter needs 77.85 cm, more than 60 cm. At 1 cm per 10^11 m Jupiter is at 7.785 cm but Mercury is only 0.579 cm from the Sun. At 1 cm per 2 × 10^10 m Mercury is at 2.895 cm and Jupiter at 38.925 cm, so both conditions hold: choose 1 cm for every 2 × 10^10 m.
s: Part (d): 2 × 10^10 m per cm, rejecting 10^10 (Jupiter off) and 10^11 (Mercury under 1 cm)

questions.q: A Rs 1 coin is about 2 × 10^-3 m thick and weighs about 4 × 10^-3 kg. The Moon is about 3.84 × 10^8 m from the Earth. (a) How many coins stacked one on another would reach the Moon? (b) What would the stack weigh, in kg? (c) With about 8 × 10^9 people in the world, how many coins would each person have to give? (d) A poster at a coin drive reads, 'If every person gave just one coin, the stack would reach the Moon.' Judge this using (c).
questions.a: (a) 3.84 × 10^8 ÷ (2 × 10^-3) = 1.92 × 10^11 coins. (b) 1.92 × 10^11 × 4 × 10^-3 = 7.68 × 10^8 kg. (c) 1.92 × 10^11 ÷ (8 × 10^9) = 24 coins each. (d) The poster is wrong: one coin each gives only 8 × 10^9 coins, 1/24 of what is needed.
s: Part (d): rejects the poster, one coin each is 1/24 of the need

questions.q:
At a senior citizens' club in 2026, a grandmother says, 'I have lived about 2.205 × 10^9 seconds.' Take 1 year ≈ 3.15 × 10^7 seconds, and take her age as a whole number of years (her birthday comes before the club function each year). The club gives a Diamond badge at its function in 2030 to every member who will have lived at least 2.4 × 10^9 seconds by then.
(a) About how old is the grandmother, in years?
(b) In about which year was she born?
(c) About how many seconds will she have lived by 2030, in scientific notation?
(d) Will she get the Diamond badge in 2030? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 2.205 × 10^9 ÷ (3.15 × 10^7) = 0.7 × 10^2 = 70 years. (b) About 2026 - 70 = 1956. (c) In 2030 she will be about 74 years old: 74 × 3.15 × 10^7 ≈ 2.33 × 10^9 seconds. (d) No: 2.33 × 10^9 is less than 2.4 × 10^9 (she needs about 76.2 years).
